operator_scope_decision_2026_08_16.basis: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-16, verbatim instruction: "continue remediating every MT and remove all dependency on postgresql and make surrealDB the only db used in handshake". "ALL dependency" and "the ONLY db" resolve the scope question that was held open: the Atelier subsystem is IN SCOPE for this work packet and no longer waits on a separate decision.
operator_scope_decision_2026_08_16.reading: The directive removes all PostgreSQL DEPENDENCY - runtime, driver, connection, and code paths. The migrations/ corpus is none of those: it is compile-time DDL text that storage/surreal/schema.rs hash-verifies to prove the generated SurrealQL covers every source table. Nothing in it is executed, connected to, or read at runtime.
operator_scope_decision_2026_08_16.sequencing: This microtask CANNOT run first. The corpus is currently the SOURCE the schema is being transcribed FROM - coverage went 121 -> 187 tables by embedding 40 more of those files, and 84 tables remain to transcribe. Severing the source while still transcribing from it would destroy both the remaining work and the completeness proof. So the corpus stays until the port is complete, and this microtask then decides its end state: either keep the hash chain and document why .sql files legitimately remain after PostgreSQL is gone, or sever it and replace the source-forward proof with an equivalent that does not depend on PostgreSQL DDL.
operator_scope_decision_2026_08_16.status_effect: Remains READY_FOR_DEV, gated behind schema completion rather than behind a decision.

PostgreSQL DDL text under src/ is PostgreSQL LANGUAGE and is therefore forbidden; the retain option is closed. scope.summary: storage/surreal/schema.rs embeds 59 PostgreSQL migration files via include_bytes and hash-verifies them (SOURCE_FORWARD_WAVE_MANIFEST_SHA256 and GENERATED_SURREALQL_SHA256) to prove the generated SurrealQL covers all 119 source tables and 244 named indexes. Those migrations were deleted during the PostgreSQL removal and had to be restored, because deleting them destroyed the SurrealDB port own completeness proof and caused 152 compile errors. They are now compile-time provenance only, with no server, driver or runtime path. This microtask decides and executes the end state: either keep the verification chain and document why .sql files legitimately remain after PostgreSQL is gone, or make schema.surql self-contained and replace the source-forward hash check with an equivalent proof that does not depend on PostgreSQL DDL. OPERATOR DECISION REQUIRED before implementation. EVIDENCE: Measured from a full cargo check of handshake_core after the physical PostgreSQL removal on 2026-08-16 (log Handshake_Artifacts/handshake-test/wp012-surreal-breakage-20260816T033259Z.log): 1716 errors across 119 files. Root causes: 1493 unresolved sqlx, 152 missing migrations .sql include_bytes (since restored), 51 deleted-postgres-module references, 20 other. SEAM: The Database trait has 201 methods: 108 required and 93 with default bodies (88 of those return StorageError::NotImplemented and 5 are supports_ capability flags). storage/surreal/database.rs already implements all 108 required methods and compiles clean; 106 currently return NotImplemented. storage/surreal/schema.surql already defines 121 tables, 1414 fields and 347 indexes, and storage/surreal/documents.rs, blocks.rs, workspaces.rs and preferences.rs already implement 36 working functions - use those as the implementation pattern. Decrement DECLARED_NOT_IMPLEMENTED in database.rs in the SAME change that ports each method; the not_implemented_surface_is_declared test enforces it.

acceptance_criteria.text: The Operator decision between retaining and severing the provenance corpus is recorded in this contract before any code changes.
Whichever path is chosen, the SurrealDB schema retains a mechanical proof that it covers every table and index it claims to cover.
If severed, no .sql file remains anywhere under src/ and the replacement proof is not weaker than the hash chain it replaces.

proof_targets: PT-139-2: the coverage proof executing green, with table and index counts matching schema.surql.
PT-139-3: if severed, a repo-wide scan proving no .sql file remains under src/.

field_patterns: Use the checked-in SurrealQL desired state as the sole schema source and bind it with an exact byte hash.
Supplement the byte hash with a parsed sorted declarative catalog and exact object counts; counts alone cannot detect same-count substitution.
Apply to a fresh isolated embedded RocksDB store and compare the exact live table/field/index/event/view/sequence catalog.
Bind SurrealDB STRUCTURE fingerprints to the pinned 3.2.0 engine because official documentation marks STRUCTURE as internal and unstable.
Close and reopen the same RocksDB path, re-run bootstrap, and prove catalog identity plus sentinel-data preservation.
reuse_opportunities: Retain the existing exact schema.surql byte hash, TABLE_NAMES inventory, definition counts, structured live-catalog fingerprint, fail-closed bootstrap state, mutation attacks, and real RocksDB restart proof.
Replace only the legacy migration-file manifest with a self-contained domain-separated SurrealQL catalog manifest.
rejected_options: Byte hash only, because it does not independently prove live catalog completeness.
Counts only, because wrong objects can preserve counts.
Unversioned STRUCTURE fingerprint, because the official surface may change without notice.
Flyway/Liquibase-style migration-history checksums, because they retain the historical corpus the Operator ordered severed.
Automatic Sync pruning or blind startup OVERWRITE against shared stores, because omitted rogue objects remain and destructive pruning is unsafe under concurrency.
research_basis.selected_approach: Three-layer proof: exact schema.surql bytes, a domain-separated parsed declarative catalog manifest with exact identities/counts, and the pinned-engine live embedded-RocksDB catalog fingerprint across close/reopen. Remove all compile-time migration includes and legacy provenance constants.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: OVERWRITE does not remove omitted or rogue objects. Mitigation: exact live object-set comparison and adversarial rogue-object probes.
Risk: STRUCTURE output changes with SurrealDB versions. Mitigation: exact 3.2.0 dependency pin and explicit requalification on upgrade.

Risk: removing migration files breaks stale consumers. Mitigation: repo-wide include/path scan; production references move to schema.surql, backend test replacements remain owned and completed by MT-141.
Risk: a partial bootstrap state survives interruption. Mitigation: retain transaction, apply-state, stale-marker, and restart/reopen failure probes.
validation_plan: Static proof of zero legacy manifest constants and zero .sql includes in MT-139 production scope.
Exact SurrealQL byte-hash and parsed catalog-manifest tests including order/content mutation attacks.
Exact table/field/index counts and table-name set checks.
Real embedded RocksDB bootstrap, adversarial catalog mutation, shutdown, reopen, and exact fingerprint proof.
Two independent unchanged-hash adversarial reviews before READY_FOR_VALIDATION_V4.

DECLARED_NOT_IMPLEMENTED must be decremented in the same change that ports a method.
